reply:
That’s a very specific fear — not that he’ll be cruel, but that he’ll switch into caretaker mode and the conversation will become about managing you instead of hearing you. And then the easy, ordinary version of the two of you feels gone.

Two things might help separate that.

One: you can name the crying before it happens. “I might cry. I’m okay. You don’t have to fix it — I just need you to listen for a minute.” That gives him a job other than “ask if you’re okay every five minutes.”

Two: you don’t have to deliver it live and perfectly. You could write it down and hand it to him, or read it. Crying while he reads is allowed. The words still get there.

But I want to ask about the last part — “it never goes back to how it was before he knew.” What is the “it” you’re afraid of losing? The ease? The way he looks at you? Something else?
